summary.en: Bandits continue to target civilians in Zamfara, abducting five children from the same family and attacking a mosque during Subhi prayer, killing Governor Dauda Lawal's aide and abducting worshippers. In Kano, thugs assaulted Kwankwaso's convoy, prompting condemnation and calls for arrests from President Obi. President Tinubu sought forgiveness for his absence after the Plateau attack and announced a five-year defence plan while AI-generated disinformation spreads ahead of the election. The conflict recorded 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Bandittene fortsetter å angripe sivile i Zamfara, kidnapper fem barn fra samme familie og angriper en moské under Subhi-bønnen, hvor de dreper en assistent til guvernør Dauda Lawal og kidnapper tilbedere. I Kano angrep gjengmedlemmer Kwankwasos følge, noe som førte til fordømmelse og krav om arrestasjoner fra president Obi. President Tinubu ba om tilgivelse for sin fravær etter angrepet i Plateau og kunngjorde en femårs forsvarsplan mens AI-generert desinformasjon sprer seg før valget. Konflikten registrerte 1 486 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
